post.title: 21 free apps built out of pure spite · September 2026
post.caption: The month's best free apps from people who got annoyed at a price tag and built the thing themselves: what each one replaces and what that used to cost.

say: two thousand six hundred and sixty-five dollars

segments.title: here we go
turns: <title><sfx whoosh>This is Spiteware Monthly. Welcome, everybody. Wherever you're watching from, I hope your month was good and your free trials got cancelled in time. I'm Vera.

<stats>Here's the deal. People get so annoyed at a price tag that they build the thing themselves and give it away. We listed {LIVE} of those in September. You're about to get the best ones: what they replace, and what that used to cost.
<eq>And I'm here because I think software should cost money.
Says the man who went through his card statement last night, <fx 🖍️ squeak>with a highlighter.
Eleven subscriptions. I recognized nine. <fx 😬 boing>One is just four capital letters and seven dollars a month.

segments.title: it used to be free
turns: <gap 0.6>Okay. First pattern. It was free, and then one day it wasn't.
<gap 0.3><bill spliit>Splitwise now caps free accounts at three expenses a day. The fourth one costs $4.99 a month.
<fx 🍝 pop>Three a day is one dinner.
<shot spliit>So Sebastien Castiel built Spliit. No limit, no account, no ads.
<fx 💬 pop tl>I'd use that. If you split bills with anybody, would you? Tell us.
<gap 0.3><bill open-photo-ai>Topaz Photo used to be a license you bought once. Now it's $39 a month. <app open-photo-ai>So vegidio built Open Photo AI.

segments.title: the last button
turns: <gap 0.7><eq>Next pattern, and it's my favorite. The price shows up at the last button.
<gap 0.3>Jareer A. finished a first video ever, clicked Export in CapCut, <bill concat>and got a popup asking for $19.99 a month.
After the whole edit. <app concat>So now there's Concat. The Export button just exports.
<bill resumake>Resume.io. $29.95, at the download button. <app resumake>Aditya Khadse built resumake. It hands you the PDF.
<fx 🔘 buzzer>Why is it always the last button?
<eq><pre meow 🐱>Sorry. That's Kerning, my cat. She has never paid for anything.

segments.title: wall of shame
turns: <gap 0.7><bill localflow><sfx drumroll>Okay. Wall of shame. The most replaced product of the month: Wispr Flow. Dictation, $15 a month. Replaced ten times.
<wall>Ten. LocalFlow, FlowLocal, FreeFlow, <wall all>and seven more.
The builder of YazSes put the grudge best: you keep paying for speech recognition that already worked the first month.
<fx 💬 pop>Anybody watching still paying for dictation? No judgment. Okay, some judgment.

segments.title: by the head
turns: <gap 0.7><eq>My turn. Per-seat pricing. I sold software for six years. A hundred people should pay more than two.
<gap 0.3>Then you'll know this one. <bill deft>Slack Pro is $8.75 a head. <app deft>Maneek21 built Deft: chat, tasks and notes on your own server.
<fx 🖥️ pop>The catch is, you run the server.

segments.title: tiny ones
turns: <gap 0.3><bill jinx>Bitly wants $10 a month to shorten a link. <app jinx>Gordon McDonald built Jinx. <fx 📄 pop>It's a text file.
<bill rescript>Descript is $24 a month to edit a video by deleting words. <app rescript>wassgha built Rescript.
<fx 📅 boing>A weekend. That used to be an eighteen-month project.

segments.title: you already own it
turns: <gap 0.7><eq>Next up: paying for things you already own.
<gap 0.3><bill openstrap-edge>WHOOP sells you a fitness band, then charges $199 a year to read it. <app openstrap-edge>OpenStrap Edge reads it anyway.
<gap 0.6><eq>Okay, this one. This one is loud.
<gap 0.3><bill yowl>Unplug Alarm wants a paid upgrade to guard your own laptop. <app yowl>nejcar20 built Yowl. Somebody grabs your MacBook, <fx 🚨 alarm>it screams.
<fx 💬 pop>Would you actually put that on your laptop? I think I would.

segments.title: on the site
turns: <gap 0.7><site apps slack>Quick site tip. The apps page has a search box. Type in whatever you're paying for, and see who already got mad about it.
I typed in Slack. I shouldn't have.
There's a manifesto on there, too.
<fx 📜 pop>I read it. The site calls seat-based pricing a hate crime. I'm trying not to take that personally.

segments.title: the expensive end
turns: <gap 0.3><bill openbot>Leonid Gorkin was paying $200 a month for Grok Bot's top tier, <fx 💸 trombone>and ran out of tokens. <app openbot>So now there's OpenBot.

There is a much bigger one. <bill openterminal>Bloomberg Terminal. $2,665 a month. <app openterminal>French Ben built OpenTerminal: a dark screen full of numbers, on your laptop, from free public data.
I would love to have been in that pricing meeting.

segments.title: spite of the month
turns: <gap 0.7><eq>Before we go. The four capital letters.
I looked it up. <fx 🧘 gong>It's a meditation app.
I've opened it twice. I'm paying seven dollars a month to be calm, <fx 😤 buzzer>and I'm furious.
Are you going to cancel it?
I'm going to try it one more time first.
That is exactly how they get you. Spite of the month. You pick.
<spite concat><sfx fanfare>Concat. Nobody planned to build a video editor that day. A popup made that decision.
<eq>I still think software should cost money. Just tell me the price before I've done all the work.
That's the most reasonable thing you've ever said to me. <outro>Everything we mentioned is linked below, and there are {MORE} more from September at spiteware.ai.
Tell us which one you'd actually use. And if a price tag ever made you build something, send it in.
<outro sub><fx 🔔 ding>And subscribe, and hit the bell, so next month's grudges come to you.
See you in November. Go and check your statement.
